The Discussion was reported to print the interval as 3.6 to 4.1; which is the typo is unresolved.
corrections.new: Unintentional drowning, global, both sexes, all ages, age-standardised rate for 2017 with 95% uncertainty interval, as printed in the Abstract and in the Results (UI: 3.8 to 4.1); 57.4% below the 1990 rate of 9.3 (8.5 to 10.0). The Discussion (second paragraph) prints the interval once as 3.6–4.1 in a passing comparison with four high-burden countries. Two of three passages, including the formal Results statement, give 3.8 to 4.1, so cite 3.8 to 4.1 and treat 3.6 as the outlier unless the IHME GBD 2017 results tool shows otherwise.

tried: The PDF reader returned only short verbatim fragments per pass and gave no character offset for the Discussion, so the full text was read in three targeted passes (Abstract/Results, Discussion sentence, then the 20 words before and 10 after the Discussion figure) rather than by offset.
notes: Both intervals are printed in the Brunel full text. 3.8 to 4.1 appears twice (Abstract, and Results first paragraph with the explicit 'UI:' label); 3.6–4.1 appears once, in the Discussion second paragraph, inside a passing comparison with China, India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. Recommendation: the lab should keep citing 4.0 (3.8 to 4.1) from the Abstract/Results; the existing figure, low and high on gbd-2017-franklin-rate are correct and need no change. The proposed corrections only update the scope and note text, which currently say the discrepancy is 'unresolved' and mention the abstract alone. Caveat: the paper itself cannot show which of the two is the typo; the consistency of Abstract and Results and the UI label make 3.8 the better-supported value, and the GBD 2017 results tool would settle it (next task). I did not check which manuscript version the Brunel copy is (accepted manuscript or version of record). Quote spacing ('per 100 000' vs 'per 100000') reflects the text extraction, not a difference in the paper. No file in the repository was edited.
